html:
The capital of Egypt, founded in 969 by the Fatimids as a walled royal city beside the older capital of Fustat. They named it al-Qahira, "the Victorious". It grew into the largest city in Africa and the Arab world.

The Fatimid general Jawhar laid it out after conquering Egypt, and the caliph moved in in 973. The mosque of Al-Azhar was built at the same time. Ordinary people and trade stayed in Fustat at first, and the two cities slowly merged. Saladin built the great Citadel and walls joining them in the 1170s.

Under the Mamluk sultans of Ayyubid and Mamluk Egypt from 1250, Cairo was the greatest city of the Islamic world, rich from the spice trade and full of mosques, schools and hospitals. Ibn Khaldun taught and died there. The Black Death struck it hard in 1348. After the Ottoman conquest of 1517 it became a provincial capital, until Egypt won back self-rule in the 19th century.
